title: Spatial density, first passage times, and entropy of run and tumble particles in a bistable potential
abstract: We study the dynamics of a run and tumble particle (RTP) in a bistable potential, in contact with a heat bath. We find the exact form of the steady state position distribution as well as its time-dependent form in Laplace space. We use this result to study relaxation properties of the spatial probability density and find that it converges to the steady state from the center outwards, with the relaxation front moving ballistically in time. Physically this ballistic behavior arises when observing relaxation properties at the tails of the density, where the distance of the particle from the origin is larger than the length-scale describing the steady state of the RTP. We also find the exact form of the mean first passage time, and the long-time behavior of the first passage time distribution. This allows us to coarse-grain the dynamics as a dichotomous Markov process, a paradigm for a wide class of bistable processes. Coarse-graining, however, comes at the cost of a loss of information: while the RTP possesses a finite entropy production even at steady state, it identically vanishes for its coarse-grained description.
summary: This paper analyzes the stochastic dynamics of a particle in a bistable potential using the Fokker-Planck framework. It derives the steady-state distribution and examines relaxation dynamics in both real and Laplace space. Crucially, it contrasts the true entropy production of the full system with that of a simplified, coarse-grained Markov process, revealing the information lost during the approximation.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics, steady-state properties, and entropy production of a Run and Tumble Particle (RTP) moving in a bistable potential coupled to a heat bath.
main_result: The analysis derives the exact steady-state probability density function and shows that while the full dynamics exhibit non-zero entropy production, a coarse-grained Markovian description incorrectly predicts zero entropy production.
method: The authors employ Fokker-Planck equations, solving them analytically in Laplace space to determine time-dependent and steady-state distributions, alongside calculating entropy production rates.
model_or_system: The model is a Run and Tumble Particle (RTP) in one dimension subjected to a bistable potential $U(x)$ and thermal noise, described by a Langevin equation and coupled Fokker-Planck equations.
key_observables: Spatial probability density function (PDF), mean first passage time, entropy production, and coarse-grained entropy.
important_parameters:
Bistable potential parameters, temperature (T), and the noise parameters ($
u_0, r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on solving the FPEs in different spatial regions and assumes the coarse-graining process is valid for large barrier heights.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of the PDF relaxing to steady state, and comparisons are made between analytical, numerical, and coarse-grained estimates of entropy over time.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first solving the steady-state FPEs, then analyzing the time-dependent PDF using Laplace transforms, and finally comparing the full dynamics' entropy production against a simplified, coarse-grained Markovian description.
why_interesting: The comparison between the full system's non-zero entropy production and the coarse-grained model's zero production highlights fundamental information loss when simplifying complex stochastic dynamics, which is relevant for open quantum systems modeling.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
